input.quote: 7.2 Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 (the first of two clauses numbered 7.2) imposes an MFN running against us: we must extend Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms we give any other technology supplier. It is unlimited as to product, duration, and comparison methodology, so it falls in walk-away territory and fails every fallback element (defined product, 12-month cap, like-for-like carve-outs). Section 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment contradicts but does not cure the operative obligation, so we take the preferred position and remove the Customer-side MFN. No Vendor-granted MFN in our favour exists to preserve.

ops.oldText: Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.
ops.newText: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We replaced Section 7.2's open-ended obligation to give Vendor the best terms we offer any other technology supplier with a statement that we owe Vendor no most-favoured-nation obligation, consistent with our playbook and with Section 12.3.
proposal.summary: Remove the Customer-side MFN obligation in Section 7.2

mappings.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
